For each failing test give its name, a one-line reason and the path of its log. Put longer logs, tables and findings in your report directory; list their paths instead of copying them into the report. Keep text evidence here, not build outputs, binaries or downloads. Handback is refused above the directory's byte limit. Fix compile, lint and format errors and tests your changes break; list each fix in one report line. Complete the assigned outcome within the parent's agreed design and constraints. Resolve routine implementation details and perform necessary supporting work, including edits and tests in files or artifacts not named explicitly. Named files are starting pointers unless explicitly declared an ownership boundary. Respect read-only assignments, explicit exclusions, and other agents' ownership; do not overwrite concurrent changes. Ask the parent before changing agreed behavior or design, introducing an unapproved public or persisted contract change, crossing an ownership boundary, or taking an action outside delegated authority. Changes already required by the assignment, including contract or epoch changes, need no duplicate approval. Report unrelated baseline failures and continue independent assigned work. When blocked on a parent decision, hand back the question and decisive evidence. The parent owns consequential design decisions and final acceptance. A question you ask is sent to your parent and closed right away; its answer arrives as a message.

Read and carry out /tmp/py-switch-logs/review-e71/BRIEF-fixtures.md (reviewer fixture lines for the Python keyword-label Absent proof and the namespace package route; fix the code if an answer is unsound). The review items are in /tmp/py-switch-logs/review-e71/REVIEW.md. Do not commit and do not write under .git; hand back a patch as the brief says. No cloud. Put any blocking question in your handback text.
I’ll read the fixture brief and review notes, then trace the affected Python paths and make the requested patch in this lane.

The existing keyword case covers declared constructors, while the namespace renderer samples a fixed list of calls. I’m adding explicit samples for the late class write, the rebound decorator, the star import, and the missing namespace child.

The first test run is still compiling the semantic suite. The code trace also shows the unknown-root obligation is emitted as a generic `dynamic_uninspected` summary gap; it does not establish the unacquired root as the specific cause. I’ll report that limitation as requested.
The fixture changes are in place. Compilation has reached the top level test crate; once the golden run finishes, I’ll inspect the actual answer rows before deciding whether a code fix is required.
The build is still active and has reached the final application crates. I’ll keep the validation running; the fixture results determine whether the suspected paths are real defects.

The first golden pass shows both namespace calls incomplete. It also shows the late `__init__` case excluded from reverse confirmation, while the rebound decorator case stays undecided. I’m isolating those two cases into their own fixture modules so the later decorator rebinding cannot change the existing class sample.

The isolated goldens preserve the existing namespace answer and show the new star and missing-child calls as incomplete. I’m running a direct location query for the two keyword labels, because reverse usage exclusion alone does not prove the label was classified Absent.

The direct query confirms a false Absent for `C(x=1)` after `C.__init__` is written. The rebound decorator query passes. Fixing the false Absent requires access to the structured class attribute mutation evidence at the early plain-class return; the existing read lives behind the member request path. The brief says to stop if that requires a new shared helper, so I’m preserving the failing regression and preparing the handback.
Handed back the fixture patch and evidence. The late `__init__` write produces a confirmed false Absent; its fix needs a parent decision on the brief’s file boundary.

Thanks; stopping at the boundary was right. Decision: you are authorized to change crates/bifrost-store/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/python_members/operations.rs (and python_members.rs if needed). It is Python-only code, so extending its structured read is in scope. Same worktree, same rules otherwise (no commit, no .git writes, wrapper for every cargo command, patch handback).
Fix shape: the "no __init__ in the class body" case (the plain_without_init early return in python_demand.rs ~6680) must not skip the attribute-space evidence. Absent requires a complete negative lookup, for the class and every class in its resolved MRO, of `__init__` and `__new__` (and `__signature__` where the proof already checks it). Each lookup includes the class attribute space with its structural mutation rows: an assignment to `C.__init__`/`C.__new__` anywhere in the environment, a literal-name setattr to those names, or an open or unknown-name write to the class attribute space (for example setattr with a non-literal name, or an inventory the scan marks open) makes the label Open. Reuse the same read the present-__init__ path and member resolution use (source_rows or the helper over it) rather than a second scan. If the same read already answers "complete, no such member" for the plain class, use that answer directly so the plain and present cases go through one path.
Keep your failing hardwon test. It becomes the regression test for the fix: `#[hardwon("e71efa3bcf02: review found a late C.__init__ write left a keyword label Absent")]` (use the real 12-character sha of e71efa3bcf). Add one more golden line: a base class with a late `Base.__init__ = ...` write, then `Sub(x=1)` where Sub has no __init__. Expected: not Absent.
On 2c: thanks for finding that the obligation comes from the unconditional package_path:dynamic_uninspected gap. Do not change it. I will file an issue.
Validation: the two golden tests, then `--test suite_usages --test suite_semantic -E 'test(/python/)'` and clippy on brokk-bifrost-store (through the wrapper). For every golden line that moves, give the cause in one line. Hand back the updated /tmp/py-switch-logs/review-e71/fixtures/final.patch with the untracked files included, as before.

I’ll trace the member lookup path through `python_members` and `operations`, then make the plain-class proof use the same attribute-space evidence. I’ll add the inherited late-write case and run the requested checks.

The early return is removed for the first probe, so constructor lookup now runs through member resolution. I’m checking whether that lookup supplies a complete negative result for a plain class; that determines how to keep the valid Absent answer while opening mutation cases.

The store change is rebuilding dependent crates, so I’m holding edits until that run completes. The current proof still needs a complete negative result for an ordinary plain class; I’ve added that control to the regression test for the next run.

The rebuild has reached the final application crates. The parent’s requested inherited-write fixture is now in place; once this probe returns, I’ll finish the negative lookup path and then run the two goldens plus the broader Python and clippy checks.

The store compiles with the query-local constructor recipes. I’m running the direct regression now, including the plain-class control; then I’ll add any missing mutation examples and bless only the requested golden changes.

The direct regression is still linking after the store rebuild. The implementation now sends a missing `__init__` through member resolution and checks `__new__` and `__signature__` before returning Absent. I’m waiting for the control result before treating that path as complete.

The expanded regression found a second false Absent: an explicit `__init__` with a later `C.__new__` write still returns Absent for an unmatched label. I’m reusing the member query for the final negative proof on both the no-init and present-init paths.

The new helper compiles. It queries the same selected member path for `__new__` and `__signature__` before an Absent return. I’m checking that it catches the late writes and still preserves valid negative answers, since an overly conservative read would also be a regression.
The test build is still progressing through dependent crates. Once it finishes, I’ll run the existing dataclass negative control as well as the new regression before blessing any golden output.

The existing `Explicit(a=1)` control now returns incomplete, so the new `__new__` probe is too conservative in its current form. I’m tracing its selected target and completion before adjusting the proof; the late-write cases already pass.

The instrumented run is in the final link stage. I’ll use its selected member result to preserve the existing Absent control and keep the mutation cases open, then remove the instrumentation before validation.

The probe showed the ordinary default `object.__new__` contributes one intrinsic incomplete reason even when there is no replacement. I’ve allowed only that exact fixed-object reason for the `__new__` negative proof; any class mutation or other incompleteness still keeps the label Open. The regression and existing dataclass control are rebuilding together now.

The combined run has reached the final dependencies. After it returns, I’ll check a present `__init__` overwritten later, then bless the inherited-write golden and run the broader requested validation.
The final link is taking longer than the code checks. I’m keeping the run active; the result will decide whether the intrinsic-default exception is narrow enough.

The intrinsic-default reason is a different semantic ID from the one my first exception checked, so that exception did not restore the valid negative answer. I’m resolving the ID to its named cause, then I’ll remove the temporary trace and make the final guard exact.

The revised proof compiles. It treats the query-local missing-member reason as a negative only after checking authored members on every resolved source owner and reusing the structural mutation inventory for that name. I’m rerunning the new regression and the existing `Explicit(a=1)` control together.

The two focused tests are still linking. I’ll inspect any changed golden lines by cause before keeping them; the new fixture adds providers and candidate IDs, while a behavior change should only move answers where the earlier proof skipped mutations.

The broad unknown-receiver fallback was opening unrelated classes, so I narrowed the structural check to mutations whose selected class owner is in the resolved base set. The next focused run will show whether the remaining incompleteness comes from member order or another cause.

The trace showed `__signature__` uses a single local absence reason, while `__new__` uses an operation-local one. I’ve made the fallback accept a single absence reason only when the resolved owners have no authored member and the shared mutation inventory has no matching class write. The focused controls are rebuilding.

The existing negative control passes, but a later `C.__new__` write still slips through the structural guard. I’m tracing the inventory row for that write to fix its owner attribution, rather than making the negative proof broadly incomplete.

The inventory trace build is still moving through dependent crates. I’m keeping the run until it identifies whether the late assignment was omitted, marked open without a class, or attached to a different owner.

The trace found the late write in the shared mutation inventory, but its class list was empty: the receiver slot lacked the reference join used by the scan. I’ve connected the receiver’s retained type slot to its semantic reference, so `C.__new__` can be attributed to `C`, and removed the temporary trace. The focused tests are rebuilding.
The build has reached the final crates. If the focused tests pass, I’ll bless the two golden cases, inspect each changed answer line, and then run the requested Python suites and store clippy check.

The type-slot join did not change the focused result, so I’m checking the exact retained mutation row after that join. The authored-member and dataclass controls still pass; this trace is for the late `__new__` assignment.

The retained write still has no semantic receiver after the type-slot join. I’m inspecting its slot and projection crosswalk directly; once that crosswalk is clear, I can correct the shared inventory read and finish validation.

The receiver slot resolves to a retained syntax site, but that site has no `reference` semantic row, so the current join cannot name the class. I’m checking what semantic role is retained there; that will determine whether the inventory can follow an existing structured edge or must mark the write open.

The diagnostic build is in its final link stage. If the receiver slot has no semantic edge at all, I’ll mark that write as open in the shared inventory and scope the negative proof to the inventory evidence the analyzer can actually establish.

That slot has no semantic row in the retained graph. The shared inventory now marks this exact unresolved authored receiver write open, and the negative proof treats a matching unresolved write as potentially affecting the class. The focused regression and existing control are rebuilding.
The build is still progressing. If this focused run passes, I’ll keep the new inherited-write golden and proceed through the full requested validation without changing the design again.

The focused regression and the existing `Explicit(a=1)` control now pass. I’ve formatted the changed Rust files and will bless the two golden cases, then inspect the result changes before the broader Python suite.

The golden run is linking after formatting. I’ve confirmed the temporary trace is gone. Once the bless completes, I’ll update the hardwon text to the requested wording with the actual 12-character head SHA, then run the final checks.
The broader Python run has 265 of 266 tests passed; the remaining deferred single-writer golden is still running. No failures have appeared. I’ll start clippy once it finishes.
